summary: We have designed a 2D game that solves the problem to the challenge: students have few opportunities to interactively explore space mission design and understand how technical decisions and limited resources affect mission success. The game turns these abstract concepts into a hands-on experience where they can test different choices and observe their consequences. Our solution is a simulation-adventure game based on real data from the Apollo 11 mission. By making engineering decisions and managing limited resources, players explore how their choices affect the success of a space mission. Along the way, they discover fascinating facts about the Moon mission and learn how to manage a limited budget in critical situations.
details: Our project is an educational game that allows players to experience the challenges of NASA engineers during the Space Race and the Apollo program. Players make decisions, manage resources and complete missions while learning about the history of space exploration. The main benefits are developing critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making skills while making learning more interactive and enjoyable. Our goal is to encourage students to become more interested in science, technology and history. We developed the game using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with the help of Claude Code, which assisted us in generating and improving the code. The creative aspect of our project comes from combining historical events with interactive gameplay, allowing players to learn through their own decisions rather than simply reading information. Throughout development, our team considered historical accuracy, educational value, game difficulty, accessibility and user experience, making sure the final result would be both entertaining and informative.
